messages:
Emma: heads-up — sales just forwarded a contract ask from Acme: they want 99.99% monthly uptime for eu regions + p95 latency <= 120ms for chat/text-gen routes. sales attached clause and requested 8-week go-live. link: https://acme.example/contract
Olivia: yep, I'm the AE on this. client is pushing enterprise tier + 24/7 support. want to know if we can commit or offer scoped alternative.
Raj: tagging product intake. need quick triage: is this an uplift of existing SLA or a brand new commitment? what routes are in scope?
Olivia: uplift. they want the stricter SLA only for 3 routes (chat-stream, summarize, document-qa). all other routes remain standard.
Maria: 99.99 is a step change. To get there we need multi-region active-active, synthetic probes, faster failover, and stricter autoscaling. rough infra uplift: ~2-3x for critical capacity, plus oncall staffing.
Emma: could we propose a scoped rollout: offer 99.99 only on "pinned customer routes" to limit cost?
Raj: framing options for sales/contract negotiation: 
Option A (Full enterprise): 99.99 across agreed endpoints, active-active in eu-west+eu-north, 24/7 oncall, SLA credits, legal signoff.
Option B (Scoped guaranteed): 99.99 only for pinned routes (customer-specified route ids), with explicit fallback behavior for non-pinned traffic. Lower price and faster delivery.
Liam: for escalation routing, propose policy: first alert -> CS on PD (15m), if customer-impacting persists -> eng-oncall (30m), then infra leads + account exec (2h). I can draft a PD policy.
Anna: legal: we'll need to see exact SLA language, availability measurement method, and the credit calculation. also request limits on liability and a termination trigger for repeated missed SLAs.
Raj: product acceptance criteria (draft): 1) automated synthetic checks from 3 AZs in each region; 2) end-to-end p95 latency tests under representative load; 3) deployment canary + automatic rollback; 4) SLA dashboard with alerting and on-call runbook; 5) one successful DR failover test.
Maria: eng tasks (high level): HA gateway, regional KV replication, shared KV quorum for cache, health-check topology, circuit breakers and graceful degradation, load-shed policy, and autoscaler tuning. will need spike to validate 120ms p95 target for the model and sequence lengths.
Emma: next steps: 1) Sales to confirm which exact routes to pin and timeline; 2) Legal to draft contract wording; 3) Eng to estimate LOE & do feasibility spike; 4) Product to create intake ticket and assign owner.
Raj: I'll create the intake ticket and label it enterprise-sla-intake. placeholder JIRA: INF-3729 (to be replaced after creation). will include acceptance criteria and owners.
Olivia: I'll ask the customer if they'll accept Option B (scoped) if Option A cost is too high. they said timeline is flexible by a few weeks if necessary.
Maria: FYI if they insist on full 99.99 across all routes with 120ms p95, realistic delivery could be 4-6 months depending on infra hires and capacity commitments.
deploy-bot: No deployments scheduled. No action until ticket INF-3729 is created and owners assigned.
Emma: scheduling quick sync at 13:15 today to finalize which option to pursue and owners. :thumbsup:
